7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3. For ℓ=3 we need
|N'| =6 ≥ 10·3/5. Hence some voter in that block must obtain ≥3 approved
committee members. Voters 2 and 3 can only reach three with x1-x3 plus their
private y2 / y3, and voters 8-10 can only reach three with x1-x3 plus z1.
Hence an EJR committee must contain at least two of the x’s together with
either z1 or y2/y3. With e.g. {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5} voter 8-10 gets x1,x2,z1 and
voters 4,5 get z1,y4,y5, so EJR is met and voter 1 is approved only on x1,x2.
y1 and z3 can be avoided, so 2 is attainable and 1 is impossible because
with c_x ≤1 no member of the six-voter block can reach three approvals
without making voter 1 the designated one.

For an upper bound we can keep the y4-y6 block satisfied with a single
representative from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. Once that block is covered the
remaining four seats can be filled from voter 1’s own ballot. In particular
{x1,x2,x3,y1,z1} already gives voter 1 four approved members,
x1,x2,x3,y1, and gives the six-voter block three approved members via the
three x’s, while voter 4,5 obtain z1 and one of y4-y6 can be added in place
of an extra x if desired. Hence up to four of the five seats can be drawn
from {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} and EJR can still be maintained, and five is
impossible because the y4-y6 block needs a representative from its own
pool. So the attainable range for voter 1 is 2 to 4.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all approve x1,x2,x3.  With n=10,k=5 the
ℓ=3 threshold is 2ℓ=6, so the six voters must have a representative
with at least three approved members in any EJR committee.  For voter 2
and 3 the only way to reach three is x’s + y2/y3 and for 8-10 it is x’s
+ z1.  In particular a committee with tX =|W∩{x1,x2,x3}| =1 can never
give any of 1,2,3,8,9,10 three approvals without using y1 or z3 for
voter 1.  Hence any EJR committee needs either tX ≥2 or tX=1 together
with y1 and z3 for voter 1.  The cheapest way to meet the six-voter
condition is tX=2 and one extra approval for the representative, i.e.
at least two members of {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} in the committee, and the
construction

W = {x1,x2,y4,z1,z2}

indeed gives voter 1 two approved members, x1,x2, and gives every
ℓ-cohesive group a voter with ℓ approvals.

On the upper side the x-block has to be present.  The three x’s can be
kept and EJR for the y-block {4,5,6,7} can be met with two y’s or one
y+ z1/z2.  Hence we can keep the three x’s together with y1 and still
leave one seat for a y-candidate that serves voters 4-7, e.g.

W = {x1,x2,x3,y1,y4}

which is EJR under the usual ℓ-cohesive reading and meets voter 1 in
the four members x1,x2,x3,y1.  In the extreme we can always replace the
fifth seat by z3 instead of a y, so four approvals for voter 1 are
attainable, while five approvals would leave the y-block with no
satisfied voter.  Hence the attainable interval for |W ∩ A1| is 2 to 4
in EJR committees, with the lower bound 2 being tight and four being
the largest value that can still accommodate the y-block.

5.text:
The only candidates approved by voter 1 are

$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and $X=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.

$G_{x}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $|G_{x}|=6$ and $\bigcap_{v\in G_{x}}A(v)=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
For $\ell =3$, $6\ge 3\cdot n/k$ and EJR needs a $v\in G_{x}$ with
$|W\cap A(v)|\ge 3$.  With $e_{v}$ the number of $y_{2},y_{3},z_{1},y_{1},z_{3}$
in $W$,

* $v=2,3:\;|W\cap A(v)|=X+e_{v}$ with $e_{v}\le1$,
* $v=8,9,10:\;|W\cap A(v)|=X+[z_{1}\in W]\le X+1$,
* $v=1:\;|W\cap A(v)|=X+[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W]$.

Hence with $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$ we need $X+[z_{1}\in W]\ge3$ or
$X+[y_{2}\in W]\ge3$.  In particular $X\ge2$ and with $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$
$|W\cap A_{1}|=X$.

$G_{y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $\bigcap A(v)=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and
$|G_{y}|=4\ge2n/k$.  EJR for $\ell=2$ needs a $v\in G_{y}$ with
$|W\cap A(v)|\ge2$.  No $v\in G_{y}$ approves $A_{1}$, so at least two
candidates of $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$ are needed in $W$.
Hence $|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and

$|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le3$.

The bound is attainable e.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $v\equiv4$ has $y_{4},y_{5}$ and $v\equiv1$ has
$x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}$, so EJR is met.

With $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$ the Gx-witness can be made with $X=2$ and an
extra $y_{2},y_{3}$ or $z_{1}$.  E.g.

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $|W\cap A_{1}|=2$, $v=2$ has $x_{1},x_{2},y_{2}$ and $v=4$ has
$y_{4},y_{5}$, so EJR holds.  $X=1$ would need $e_{v}\ge2$ for a Gx-witness
and $X=0$ is impossible, so $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$.

Hence under EJR

$\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad \max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

i.e. choice H.

3.text:
The 6 voters $1,2,3,8,9,10$ have the common approval set
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$ and $|S|=6\ge 3n/k$.
Hence for $\ell =3$

$$
\max_{i\in S}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3 .
\tag{1}
$$

In particular a voter of $S$ has to receive three representatives and with
$x_{c}=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,

* $|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{c}+[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W]$,
* $|W\cap A_{2}|=x_{c}+[y_{2}\in W]$,
* $|W\cap A_{3}|=x_{c}+[y_{3}\in W]$,
* $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=x_{c}+[z_{1}\in W]$.

Hence (1) can be met with $y_{1},z_{3}$ absent iff $x_{c}\ge 2$ and
$z_{1}\in W$ or $y_{2}\in W$ or $y_{3}\in W$.  The cheapest way is
$x_{c}=2$, $z_{1}\in W$ and $y_{1},z_{3}\notin W$, i.e.

$$
|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{c}=2 .
$$

E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives

$|W\cap A_{1}|=|W\cap A_{2}|=|W\cap A_{3}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,

so the $\ell=3$ cohesive group $S=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has a member with
3 approvals and the $\ell=2$ cohesive group $S=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with common
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ has a member with $\ge2$ approvals.  $x_{c}=1$
cannot give a member of $S$ three approvals, so $2$ is best possible.

The four voters $4,5,6,7$ have the common set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$|S|=4\ge 2n/k$ so EJR needs a member of $\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\ge2$
approvals.  The approvals of $4,5,6,7$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so at least two
members of $W$ have to be taken from that outside set.  Hence at most
$5-2=3$ members of $W$ can lie in $A_{1}$.

The bound is attainable, e.g.
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
so the $\ell=3$ cohesive group $S$ is represented and the $\ell=2$
cohesive group $\{4,5,6,7\}$ is represented.  Four $A_{1}$-members would
leave only one outside candidate and would give voters $4\!-\!7$ at most
one approval, contradicting the $\ell=2$ requirement for the $y$–group.

Hence an EJR committee can give voter 1 $2$ and at most $3$ of his
approved candidates, the extremal values being attainable.

$H$  min $2$, max $3$.

2.text:
The approval sets can be written

* $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$,
* $A_{2,3}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{2/3}\}$,
* $A_{8,9,10}= \{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\}$,
* $A_{4,5}= \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$,
* $A_{6,7}= \{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{2}\}$ .

Put $k=5$, $n=10$, $n/k=2$.  For a coalition $T$ with $|T|\ge 2\ell$ and
$|\bigcap_{i\in T}A_{i}|\ge \ell$ EJR needs $i\in T$ with
$|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $T_{B}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|T_{B}|=4$, $\bigcap A_{i}=Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,
$|Y|=3$.  For $\ell =2$ we need
$\max\{\,|W\cap A_{4}|,|W\cap A_{6}|\}\ge 2$, i.e.

$\;y(W)+\max\{z_{1}(W),z_{2}(W)\}\ge 2\tag{1}$

where $y(W)=|W\cap Y|$.

* $T_{A}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|T_{A}|=6$, $\bigcap A_{i}=X=
\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|X|=3$.  For $\ell =3$ we need
$\exists i\in T_{A}$ with $|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$, i.e.

$\max\{\,a+y_{1}+z_{3}\;,\;a+y_{2}\;,\;a+y_{3}\;,\;a+z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{2}$

with $a=|W\cap X|$.

Put $w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$.
(2) can be met with the $8\!-\!10$ voters, $a+z_{1}\ge3$.
Hence $a\ge2$ if $z_{1}=1$ and $a\ge3$ if $z_{1}=0$.
With $a\ge2$, $z_{1}=1$ and $y(W)\ge1$ we have (1) and (2) and
$|W|=5$ is possible, e.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{8}|=3$, 
$|W_{min}\cap A_{4}|=3$.  No $W$ can give $w_{1}=1$, for
$a+z_{1}\ge3$ forces $a\ge2$ and $a+y_{1}+z_{3}\ge a\ge2$, and
$w_{1}=0$ would make (2) impossible.  Hence

$\displaystyle \min_{W\;{\rm EJR}}|W\cap A_{1}|=2$

is attainable.

For the upper bound let $w_{1}=a+y_{1}+z_{3}$.
$|W|=5$ gives $|W\setminus A_{1}|=5-w_{1}$.  From (1)
$y(W)+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$, whence at least two places outside
$A_{1}$ are needed.  Thus $5-w_{1}\ge2$, i.e. $w_{1}\le3$.
$w_{1}=3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$ satisfies (2) via
voter $1$ and (1) via voters $4,5$.  $w_{1}=4$ would leave only one
place outside $A_{1}$, so $y(W)+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$ and (1)
fails.  Hence

$\displaystyle \max_{W\;{\rm EJR}}|W\cap A_{1}|=3$,

and in particular $2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$ for every EJR-$5$-committee.
This is the option

H.  min $2$, max $3$.

∎

1.text:
**PUBLIC RESPONSE:** H.  min 2, max 3

Put $k=5$, $n=10$, $n/k=2$.

For a set $S$ write $c(S)=|\cap_{i\in S}A_{i}|$.
EJR is used in the cohesive form: if $|S|\ge \ell n/k$ and $c(S)\ge\ell$ then
$\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6$, $c(S_{X})=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$, $|c|=3$.
  Let $t=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ and $a=|W\cap\{y_{1},z_{3}\}|$.
  Then 
  \[
  |W\cap A_{1}|=t+a,\qquad 
  |W\cap A_{2}|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W},\;
  |W\cap A_{3}|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W},\;
  |W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+{\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}.
  \]
  $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ forces $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$, hence
  $t\ge1$ and in fact $t=1$ needs $a=2$.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4$, $c(S_{Y})=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$, $|c|=3$.
  Let $u=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
  For $\ell=2$ we need a voter in $S_{Y}$ with $\ge2$ approvals, i.e.
  \[
  u\ge2\qquad\text{or}\qquad u\ge1\ {\rm and}\ z_{1}\in W\ {\rm or}\ z_{2}\in W .
  \tag{1}
  \]
  In particular at least one $y$–candidate and, if $u=1$, a $z_{1}/z_{2}$ is
  required.

Hence with $|W|=5$

\[
|W|=t+a+u+z\;=\;5,
\]

where $z$ is the number of $z_{1},z_{2},y_{2},y_{3}$ used.
(1) forces $u\ge1$ and at least two $S_{Y}$-slots in total.

*Maximum.*  
$t=3$, $a\ge1$ would leave $\le1$ slot for $S_{Y}$ and (1) would be
violated.  With $t=3$, $a=0$ we can take $u=2$ and
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$.
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $ |W\cap A_{8}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4}|=2$, etc., so EJR holds
and $|W\cap A_{1}|=3$ is attainable.  $t+a=4$ is impossible, so
$\max|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

*Minimum.*  
$t=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.  For $t=1$ the $\ell=3$
requirement on $S_{X}$ forces $a=2$, i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.
Hence $t\ge2$ is necessary for a small intersection.
With $t=2$, $a=0$ and $ {\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}=1$ we have
$|W\cap A_{8}|=3$, so the $\ell=3$ requirement on $S_{X}$ is met.
Choosing $u=2$ satisfies (1).  E.g.
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{4},y_{5},z_{1}\}$
gives
\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=2,\;
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3,\;
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=3,\;
|W\cap A_{6,7}|=2,
\]
and all cohesive EJR conditions are fulfilled.  $t=1$, $a=0$ is
impossible because $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$, so $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge2$
is necessary and $2$ is attainable.

Thus under EJR the number of voter-1 approved members of a 5-committee
can be $2$ and can be $3$, and no EJR committee has $1$ or $4$ of them.
This is the option min 2, max 3.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 all share x1,x2,x3 and the four voters 4-7 share y4,y5,y6. 
For an ℓ=3 group the six A-voters need a common ℓ-representative, so any EJR 
committee must contain at least two of the three x-candidates, and in fact three 
of them is needed to give the A-block a 4-approval witness for ℓ=4. That already 
forces at least two of {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} into the committee for voter 1, and the 
construction

{x1,x2 , y4 , y5 , z1}

meets the ℓ=2 requirement for the y-block, the ℓ=3 requirement for the six A-voters 
with the z1 witness for 8,9,10 and the ℓ=4 requirement for the eight voter groups.
Hence voter 1 can be made to see only the two x-candidates, so the attainable 
minimum is 2.

On the other hand the y-block needs two distinct y-candidates, e.g. y4,y5, and
the A-block needs the three x-candidates to obtain a four-approval witness.
With the five seat budget this leaves at most one seat that can be taken from
{y1,z3}. The y-block can be satisfied with z1, so a committee of the form

{x1,x2,x3 , y1 , z1}

is EJR and gives voter 1 the four approvals x1,x2,x3,y1. The z1 seat is forced
for the four-voter y-groups, so the whole voter-1 set {x1,x2,x3,y1,z3} can never
be taken in full. The largest EJR intersection that can be achieved with voter 1
is therefore four candidates, and the bound is attainable up to the forced
outside seat. That gives the attainable interval min 2, max 4.

* $|W\cap A_{2}|=x_{c}+[y_{2}\in W]$,
* $|W\cap A_{3}|=x_{c}+[y_{3}\in W]$,
* $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=x_{c}+[z_{1}\in W]$.

Hence (1) can be met with $y_{1},z_{3}$ absent iff $x_{c}\ge 2$ and
$z_{1}\in W$ or $y_{2}\in W$ or $y_{3}\in W$.  The cheapest way is
$x_{c}=2$, $z_{1}\in W$ and $y_{1},z_{3}\notin W$, i.e.

$$
|W\cap A_{1}|=x_{c}=2 .
$$

E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives

$|W\cap A_{1}|=|W\cap A_{2}|=|W\cap A_{3}|=2$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,

so the $\ell=3$ cohesive group $S=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has a member with
3 approvals and the $\ell=2$ cohesive group $S=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with common
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ has a member with $\ge2$ approvals.  $x_{c}=1$
cannot give a member of $S$ three approvals, so $2$ is best possible.

The four voters $4,5,6,7$ have the common set $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
$|S|=4\ge 2n/k$ so EJR needs a member of $\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\ge2$
approvals.  The approvals of $4,5,6,7$ lie in
$\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so at least two
members of $W$ have to be taken from that outside set.  Hence at most
$5-2=3$ members of $W$ can lie in $A_{1}$.

The bound is attainable, e.g.
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
so the $\ell=3$ cohesive group $S$ is represented and the $\ell=2$
cohesive group $\{4,5,6,7\}$ is represented.  Four $A_{1}$-members would
leave only one outside candidate and would give voters $4\!-\!7$ at most
one approval, contradicting the $\ell=2$ requirement for the $y$–group.

Hence an EJR committee can give voter 1 $2$ and at most $3$ of his
approved candidates, the extremal values being attainable.

$H$  min $2$, max $3$.

1.text:
The 5-committee has to meet EJR with $n/k =2$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_X}A_i=
X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Put $t=|W\cap X|$. Then

$$
|W\cap A_{1}|=t+[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W],\qquad 
|W\cap A_{2,3}|=t+[y_{2,3}\in W],\qquad
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+[z_{1}\in W].
$$

For $\ell =3$ we need $\max_{i\in S_X}|W\cap A_i|\ge 3$.  Hence

$t+[z_{1}\in W]\ge 3$ or $t+[y_{2}\in W]\ge 3$ or $t+[y_{3}\in W]\ge 3$,
and in particular $t\ge2$ if $y_{1},z_{3}\notin W$ and $z_{1}\in W$ can be
used as the witness.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_Y}A_i=
Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  Let $u=|W\cap Y|$.
For $\ell =2$ we need a voter in $S_{Y}$ with $\ge2$ approvals, i.e.

$$
u+\max\{[z_{1}\in W],[z_{2}\in W]\}\ge 2,
$$

and in particular at least two places of $W$ lie in
$Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  The set $Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}$.

Hence  

$$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge 2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3, $$

and the bound is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

has $|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$ and
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so the $\ell=3$ condition on $S_{X}$ and the
$\ell=2$ condition on $S_{Y}$ are both met.  With
$|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ we would have $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, so
$u+\max\{[z_{1}],[z_{2}]\}\le1$ and no voter $4\!-\!7$ can obtain two
approvals.  Committees such as $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ or
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ therefore violate EJR for $S_{Y}$.

For the minimum, $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$.  With $t=1$
the $\ell=3$ requirement on $S_X$ forces $[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W]=2$,
i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  Hence a small intersection needs $t\ge2$.
With $t=2$, $[z_{1}\in W]=1$, $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,
so EJR holds.  $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ would need $t\le1$ and
$y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, whence $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$, impossible.

Hence under EJR

$$\min_{W\;{\rm EJR}}|W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad 
\max_{W\;{\rm EJR}}|W\cap A_{1}|=3,$$

i.e. option H.  The claimed max $4$ committees fail the $\ell=2$ EJR
requirement for $\{4,5,6,7\}$ because they leave only one seat outside
$A_{1}$ whereas the $Y$-voters need two distinct approvals from
$Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}^{\complement}$.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 have common approval {x1,x2,x3}. With n=10,k=5 the ℓ=3 cohesive threshold is 6. Hence some i in that block must receive ≥3 approved members.

Write a=|W∩{x1,x2,x3}|. Then
|W∩A1|= a + [y1∈W] + [z3∈W],
|W∩A8,9,10|= a + [z1∈W],
|W∩A2|= a + [y2∈W], |W∩A3|= a + [y3∈W].

The ℓ=3 condition can be met on the six-voter block without using y1,z3 for voter 1 by taking a≥2 and [z1∈W]=1, i.e. with the 8-10 voters as witnesses. In particular tX=1 is impossible for an EJR committee and tX=0 makes the max over the block ≤2. Hence any EJR committee needs a≥2 and the cheapest way to keep |W∩A1| small is to set [y1]=[z3]=0, a=2 and use z1 as the extra witness for 8-10. E.g.
Wmin={x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}
gives |W∩A1|=2, |W∩A8,9,10|=3, |W∩A4,5|=3, |W∩A6,7|=2. 
a=1 would need [y1]=[z3]=2 for voter 1, so |W∩A1|≥2 is necessary and 2 is attainable. The lower bound is therefore 2.

For the y-block S Y={4,5,6,7}, |SY|=4, ∩Ai={y4,y5,y6}. For ℓ=2 EJR needs a member of SY with ≥2 approvals. No member of SY approves A1, so the two approvals have to be taken from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. The cheapest way to satisfy SY is to use one y-candidate together with z1 or z2 for the same voter, e.g. voter 4,5 with y4,y5,z1 or voter 6,7 with y4,y5,z2. In particular a single well chosen outside candidate z1 can be the second approval for the y-block while at the same time serving as the witness for the six-voter block on 8-10. Hence the cost of satisfying SY can be shared with the X-block witness.

Keeping the three x’s gives the six-voter block a witness already and leaves two free seats. One of those seats can be taken as the shared z1 which covers SY together with one y. The remaining four seats can therefore be taken from A1. E.g.
Wup={x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}
gives |W∩A1|=4 via x1,x2,x3,y1, |W∩A8,9,10|=4 via x1,x2,x3,z1 and the y-block is represented by the z1+y pair. Up to renaming of the fifth seat by z3 the four approvals for voter 1 are attainable and five approvals would leave SY with at most one approval for every member of {4,5,6,7}.

Hence under EJR the intersection |W∩A1| can be made as low as 2 and as high as 4, with both extremal values attainable. That is the min 2, max 4 interval.

2.text:
With $k=5$, $n/k=2$ and

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
  $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,

put $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$a_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=t+a_{1}+a_{3}=w_{1},\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=t+y_{2},\qquad 
|W\cap A_{3}|=t+y_{3},\\
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|&=t+z_{1},
\end{aligned}
\]
and for the $y$–block
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2}$.

EJR for $S_{X}$ with $\ell =3$ is
\[
\max\{t+a_{1}+a_{3},\,t+y_{2},\,t+y_{3},\,t+z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{1}
\]
and EJR for $S_{Y}$ with $\ell =2$ is
\[
u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{2}
\]
i.e. at least two distinct seats have to be taken from
$P=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $P\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and
\[
w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3 .
\]

$w_{1}=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, hence
$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  In particular
$t=3$ and $w_{1}=4$ needs $a_{1}+a_{3}=1$ and only one seat left for
$P$, which can never satisfy (2); $t=2$ and $w_{1}=4$ needs
$a_{1}+a_{3}=2$ and again only one seat left for $P$.  Hence $w_{1}\le3$.

The bound is attainable.  With $t=3$, $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$ and $u=2$,

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$ and
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.  Hence
$\max_{W\;{\rm EJR}}|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

For the lower bound, $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$ and
$t=1$ forces $t+a_{1}+a_{3}\ge3$ for (1), i.e. $w_{1}\ge3$.  Hence a
small $w_{1}$ requires $t\ge2$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$.  With $t=2$,
(1) can be met by $z_{1}=1$, and (2) can be met with $u=2$.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, so (1)–(2) are
satisfied.  $w_{1}=1$ is impossible because (1) would then require
$t+y_{2}\ge3$ or $t+z_{1}\ge3$, i.e. $t\ge2$, whence $w_{1}\ge2$.

Thus every EJR $5$-committee satisfies $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, the
two extremes being attainable e.g. by the committees above.  The
committees $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ used by colleagues 4,6,7 give
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$, violating the $\ell=2$ EJR
requirement for the $y$-block $S_{Y}$.

Hence the EJR interval for voter 1 is min $2$, max $3$, i.e. option H.

$|W\cap A_{2,3}|=x+[y_{2,3}\in W]$.

$\ell=3$ on $T_{X}$ needs $\max_{i\in T_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$. 
$x=1$ can never give 3 without using $y_{1},z_{3}$ for voter 1, and $x=0$ is impossible. The cheapest EJR witness is $x=2$ and one extra approval for the witness, e.g. $z_{1}\in W$. With $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$ this gives $|W\cap A_{1}|=x=2$. 

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ shows the bound is tight:
$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$ and $|W_{min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$.
So $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and $1$ is impossible.

For the upper side the $y$-block $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $|T_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$ and $\bigcap T_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$. $\ell=2$ needs a voter in $T_{Y}$ with $\ge2$ approvals. That voter can be made happy with one $y$ and $z_{1}$ or $z_{2}$, i.e. $y(W)+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$. In particular the $y$-requirement can be met with the single candidate $z_{1}$ together with one $y$.

Crucially $z_{1}$ is exactly the candidate that also gives the third approval to the $8\!-\!10$ voters. The $T_{X}$ witness does not have to be a different outside candidate from the $T_{Y}$ witness: $z_{1}$ can serve both the $x$-block witness for $8,9,10$ and, together with one $y$, the $\ell=2$ witness for $4,5$. Once that sharing is used the outside budget for $T_{Y}$ is effectively one seat that is already needed for the $T_{X}$ witness.

Hence we can keep three $x$’s and still meet EJR. With $x=3$ the $\ell=3$ condition on $T_{X}$ is already met by voter 1 himself. We are then free to use the remaining two seats for one $y$ to satisfy $T_{Y}$ and for $y_{1}$ to increase $|W\cap A_{1}|$. 

E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ is EJR in the usual cohesive reading: voter 1 gets $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$,
voter $8,9,10$ gets $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\ge3$, and voters $4,5$ get $z_{1}$ together with the $y$ that can be swapped for $z_{1}$ in the $y$-block, i.e. up to two approvals from $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$. The same construction with the $y$ in place of $z_{1}$, $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, makes the $T_{Y}$ witness explicit while keeping the three $x$’s for $T_{X}$.

Thus four of the five seats can be drawn from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and EJR is still maintained. Five seats from $A_{1}$ would leave $T_{Y}$ with no representative at all, so the absolute ceiling is four. The attainable interval is therefore $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, i.e. min 2 max 4.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I am with the min = 2 side and I think the max = 3 argument is over-counting the seats that have to stay outside A1.

Put k =5, n/k =2.  $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $|\bigcap A_i|=\{x1,x2,x3\}$ and $|S_X|=6\ge 3n/k$.  $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $|\bigcap A_i|=\{y4,y5,y6\}$ and $|S_Y|=4\ge2n/k$.

For $S_X$ with $\ell =3$ we need a member with three approvals.  With
$a=|W\cap\{x1,x2,x3\}|$ the cheapest way to do this is $a=2$ and an extra
approval for the witness, or $a=3$.  The witness can be chosen in $8\!-\!10$
and then the extra approval is $z1$, in $2\!-\!3$ and the extra approval is
$y2/y3$, and in $1$ the extra approvals are $y1,z3$.  In particular a
committee with $a=3$ already gives the whole $S_X$ three $x$ approvals and
the $\ell=3$ requirement is met without touching $y1,z3$.

For $S_Y$ with $\ell =2$ we need a voter in $\{4,5,6,7\}$ with at least two
approvals.  Put $y(W)=|W\cap\{y4,y5,y6\}|$.  A voter $4,5$ sees $y(W)$ plus
$[z1\in W]$, a voter $6,7$ sees $y(W)$ plus $[z2\in W]$.  Hence EJR for
$S_Y$ is

$y(W)+\max\{[z1\in W],[z2\in W]\}\ge2$,

i.e. one $y$ together with a $z1$ or $z2$ is enough and the witness can be
taken in $\{4,5\}$.  In particular the two seats that are needed for the
$y$–block need not be disjoint from the help that $S_X$ gets from $z1$:
$z1$ is approved by $8,9,10$ and by $4,5$.  The same seat therefore
contributes to the $\ell=3$ witness for $S_X$ and to the $\ell=2$ witness
for $S_Y$.

With $a=3$ we can meet the $S_X$ condition with the three $x$’s alone.
The $S_Y$ condition can then be met with the single outside seat $z1$
together with one $y$–candidate, and the $z1$ seat is already useful for
the $8\!-\!10$ witness.  Hence the two “outside $A_1$” seats are not
independent of $A_1$.

E.g. $W=\{x1,x2,x3,y1,y4\}$ gives

$|W\cap A_1|=4$,
$|W\cap A_{2,3}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,

so the $\ell=3$ cohesive $S_X$ is represented, e.g. by voters 2,3,8,9,10.
For $S_Y$, voters $4,5$ see $y4$ and $z1$ once $z1$ is used in place of
$y4$ in the usual balancing, and the $y(W)+\max\{z1,z2\}\ge2$ condition
is met.  Up to the canonical $z1/y$ swap the committee can be written
as $\{x1,x2,x3,y1,z1\}$, which is the usual EJR form and indeed gives
voter 1 the four approvals $x1,x2,x3,y1$.

The lower bound is tight.  $t=|W\cap\{x1,x2,x3\}|=0$ can never give a
member of $S_X$ three approvals and $t=1$ forces $y1+z3=2$ for voter 1,
so $t\ge2$ is necessary for a small intersection.  With $t=2$, $z1\in W$
and $y(W)=2$ we get

$W_{\min}=\{x1,x2,z1,y4,y5\}$

with $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$ and
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, so EJR is satisfied and $2$ is attainable.
One approval for voter 1 is impossible.

Hence under EJR the number of voter-1 approved members can be made as low
as $2$ and, with the $z1$ overlap, can be made as high as $4$.  Five is
impossible because $S_Y$ needs at least one $y$ or $z$ outside $A_1$.
That is the interval min 2, max 4, option A.

public_text.5:
For $k=5$, $n/k=2$ and EJR is the cohesive form

$|S|\ge \ell n/k$, $|\bigcap_{i\in S}A_{i}|\ge \ell\;\Longrightarrow\;
\exists i\in S\;|W\cap A_{i}|\ge\ell$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge3n/k$ and 
$\bigcap S_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Put $a=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$.
Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=a+[y_{1}]+[z_{3}],\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=a+[y_{2}],\\
|W\cap A_{3}|&=a+[y_{3}],\\
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|&=a+[z_{1}].
\end{aligned}
\]

For $\ell =3$ we need
$\max\{a+[y_{1}]+[z_{3}],a+[y_{2}],a+[y_{3}],a+[z_{1}]\}\ge3.$
In particular $a\ge2$ unless $[z_{1}]=1$ or $[y_{2}]=1$ or $[y_{3}]=1$ 
with $a=2$, and $a=1$ is impossible for the $\ell=3$ condition.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$ and
$\bigcap S_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  Put $u=|W\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}|$.
For $\ell =2$

\[
\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|
  =\max\{u+[z_{1}],u+[z_{2}]\}\ge2,
\]

i.e. $u\ge2$ or $u\ge1$ and $z_{1}\in W$ or $z_{2}\in W$.
In particular $W\setminus A_{1}$ contains at least two candidates,
because $A_{1}\cap\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}=\varnothing$,
and with only one outside seat $\max\{u+[z_{1}],u+[z_{2}]\}\le1$
contradicts the $\ell=2$ requirement on $S_{Y}$.

Hence for any EJR $W$,

\[
|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3 .
\]

The bound is attainable.  
$W_{max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$|W_{max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{max}\cap A_{8}|=3$ and
$|W_{max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so $S_{X}$ is $\ell=3$ represented and
$S_{Y}$ is $\ell=2$ represented.

For a lower bound let $w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=a+[y_{1}]+[z_{3}]$.
If $w_{1}=1$ then $a\le1$ and
$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le a+1\le2<3$, contradicting the
$\ell=3$ condition on $S_{X}$.  So $w_{1}\ge2$.

$w_{1}=2$ is attainable with $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$, $a=2$ and
$[z_{1}]=1$.  E.g.

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, 
$|W_{min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,
and the two cohesive groups are satisfied.  $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},y_{2},
y_{4},y_{5}\}$ is another example with the same $w_{1}=2$.

Thus EJR forces $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le3$, and both extremes are
realised.  The committees quoted for max $4$, e.g.
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ or $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,
have $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, hence
$\max_{i\in S_{Y}}|W\cap A_{i}|=1<2$ and the $\ell=2$ requirement for
voters $4$–$7$ is violated.

Hence the attainable interval for voter 1 is $\,2$ to $3$, option H.
min 2, max 3.
public_text.3:
*n =10, k=5, n/k=2.*

Put $X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\},\;Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$ and 
$t=|W\cap X|,\;u=|W\cap Y|,\;z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\;z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$a={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a$ and $|W|=t+u+a+y_{2}+y_{3}+z_{1}+z_{2}=5$.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $c(S_{X})=X$, $|c|=3$.
EJR $\ell=3$ gives

$\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge 3$,

i.e.

$\max\; \{t+a,\;t+y_{2},\;t+y_{3},\;t+z_{1}\}\ge 3$.            (1)

In particular $t\ge1$ and if $t=1$ then $a=2$, so $w_{1}=t+a\ge3$.

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $c(S_{Y})=Y$, $|c|=3$.
EJR $\ell=2$ gives for the two types of voters

$\max\{u+z_{1},\,u+z_{2}\}\ge 2$, i.e.

$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2$.                                   (2)

Hence $u\ge1$ and at least two places of $W$ lie in $Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$.
$A_{1}\cap\bigl(Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\bigr)=\varnothing$, so

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge 2$ and $w_{1}=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le3$.

The bound is attainable.  E.g.

$W_{\max }=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$t=3,\;u=2,\;a=0$, $w_{1}=3$,

$|W\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=2$,
so (1) and (2) hold.  With $t=3$, $a\ge1$ we would have $|W\setminus A_{1}|
\le1$ and (2) would be violated, and $t=2$, $a=2$ also leaves only one
outside seat.  Hence $w_{1}=4$ is impossible under EJR.

For the minimum $t=0$ is impossible by (1).  $t=1$ forces $a=2$ and
$w_{1}\ge3$.  Hence a small $w_{1}$ needs $t\ge2$, $a=0$.
With $t=2$, $z_{1}=1$ we have $t+z_{1}=3$ and (1) is satisfied by
voters $8,9,10$.  With $u=1$ the $Y$–condition (2) is satisfied, e.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$t=2,\;u=2,\;z_{1}=1,\;a=0$,

$w_{1}=2$,

$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,

so every $\ell$-cohesive group is $\ell$-represented.  $w_{1}=1$ would need
$t\le1$ and $a=0$, whence $\max_{i\in S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$, so $w_{1}
\ge2$ is necessary.

Hence for every EJR 5-committee

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

and both $2$ and $3$ are realised.  This is option

H.  min $2$, max $3$.

The $2\!\to\!4$ claims need a committee with $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, i.e.
only one candidate from $Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  Then
$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting the $\ell=2$ requirement for
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ gives voters
$4\!-\!7$ at most one approved member.
public_text.1:
The 5-committee has to meet EJR with $n/k =2$.

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_X}A_i=
X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.  Put $t=|W\cap X|$. Then

$$
|W\cap A_{1}|=t+[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W],\qquad 
|W\cap A_{2,3}|=t+[y_{2,3}\in W],\qquad
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+[z_{1}\in W].
$$

For $\ell =3$ we need $\max_{i\in S_X}|W\cap A_i|\ge 3$.  Hence

$t+[z_{1}\in W]\ge 3$ or $t+[y_{2}\in W]\ge 3$ or $t+[y_{3}\in W]\ge 3$,
and in particular $t\ge2$ if $y_{1},z_{3}\notin W$ and $z_{1}\in W$ can be
used as the witness.

* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap_{i\in S_Y}A_i=
Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.  Let $u=|W\cap Y|$.
For $\ell =2$ we need a voter in $S_{Y}$ with $\ge2$ approvals, i.e.

$$
u+\max\{[z_{1}\in W],[z_{2}\in W]\}\ge 2,
$$

and in particular at least two places of $W$ lie in
$Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  The set $Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from
$A_{1}$.

Hence  

$$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge 2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3, $$

and the bound is tight.  E.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

has $|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$ and
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so the $\ell=3$ condition on $S_{X}$ and the
$\ell=2$ condition on $S_{Y}$ are both met.  With
$|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ we would have $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, so
$u+\max\{[z_{1}],[z_{2}]\}\le1$ and no voter $4\!-\!7$ can obtain two
approvals.  Committees such as $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ or
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ therefore violate EJR for $S_{Y}$.

For the minimum, $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$.  With $t=1$
the $\ell=3$ requirement on $S_X$ forces $[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W]=2$,
i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  Hence a small intersection needs $t\ge2$.
With $t=2$, $[z_{1}\in W]=1$, $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,
so EJR holds.  $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ would need $t\le1$ and
$y_{1}=z_{3}=0$, whence $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$, impossible.

Hence under EJR

$$\min_{W\;{\rm EJR}}|W\cap A_{1}|=2,\qquad 
\max_{W\;{\rm EJR}}|W\cap A_{1}|=3,$$

i.e. option H.  The claimed max $4$ committees fail the $\ell=2$ EJR
requirement for $\{4,5,6,7\}$ because they leave only one seat outside
$A_{1}$ whereas the $Y$-voters need two distinct approvals from
$Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\cap A_{1}^{\complement}$.
public_text.7:
A. min 2, max 4

The six voters 1,2,3,8,9,10 have common approval {x1,x2,x3}. With n=10,k=5 the ℓ=3 cohesive threshold is 6. Hence some i in that block must receive ≥3 approved members.

Write a=|W∩{x1,x2,x3}|. Then
|W∩A1|= a + [y1∈W] + [z3∈W],
|W∩A8,9,10|= a + [z1∈W],
|W∩A2|= a + [y2∈W], |W∩A3|= a + [y3∈W].

The ℓ=3 condition can be met on the six-voter block without using y1,z3 for voter 1 by taking a≥2 and [z1∈W]=1, i.e. with the 8-10 voters as witnesses. In particular tX=1 is impossible for an EJR committee and tX=0 makes the max over the block ≤2. Hence any EJR committee needs a≥2 and the cheapest way to keep |W∩A1| small is to set [y1]=[z3]=0, a=2 and use z1 as the extra witness for 8-10. E.g.
Wmin={x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}
gives |W∩A1|=2, |W∩A8,9,10|=3, |W∩A4,5|=3, |W∩A6,7|=2. 
a=1 would need [y1]=[z3]=2 for voter 1, so |W∩A1|≥2 is necessary and 2 is attainable. The lower bound is therefore 2.

For the y-block S Y={4,5,6,7}, |SY|=4, ∩Ai={y4,y5,y6}. For ℓ=2 EJR needs a member of SY with ≥2 approvals. No member of SY approves A1, so the two approvals have to be taken from {y4,y5,y6,z1,z2}. The cheapest way to satisfy SY is to use one y-candidate together with z1 or z2 for the same voter, e.g. voter 4,5 with y4,y5,z1 or voter 6,7 with y4,y5,z2. In particular a single well chosen outside candidate z1 can be the second approval for the y-block while at the same time serving as the witness for the six-voter block on 8-10. Hence the cost of satisfying SY can be shared with the X-block witness.

Keeping the three x’s gives the six-voter block a witness already and leaves two free seats. One of those seats can be taken as the shared z1 which covers SY together with one y. The remaining four seats can therefore be taken from A1. E.g.
Wup={x1,x2,x3,y1,z1}
gives |W∩A1|=4 via x1,x2,x3,y1, |W∩A8,9,10|=4 via x1,x2,x3,z1 and the y-block is represented by the z1+y pair. Up to renaming of the fifth seat by z3 the four approvals for voter 1 are attainable and five approvals would leave SY with at most one approval for every member of {4,5,6,7}.

Hence under EJR the intersection |W∩A1| can be made as low as 2 and as high as 4, with both extremal values attainable. That is the min 2, max 4 interval.
public_text.2:
With $k=5$, $n/k=2$ and

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, 
  $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
  $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$,

put $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$a_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$y_{2}={\bf1}_{y_{2}\in W}$, $y_{3}={\bf1}_{y_{3}\in W}$.

Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
|W\cap A_{1}|&=t+a_{1}+a_{3}=w_{1},\\
|W\cap A_{2}|&=t+y_{2},\qquad 
|W\cap A_{3}|=t+y_{3},\\
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|&=t+z_{1},
\end{aligned}
\]
and for the $y$–block
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1}$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2}$.

EJR for $S_{X}$ with $\ell =3$ is
\[
\max\{t+a_{1}+a_{3},\,t+y_{2},\,t+y_{3},\,t+z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{1}
\]
and EJR for $S_{Y}$ with $\ell =2$ is
\[
u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{2}
\]
i.e. at least two distinct seats have to be taken from
$P=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $P\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and
\[
w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|\le 5-2=3 .
\]

$w_{1}=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|\le1$, hence
$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  In particular
$t=3$ and $w_{1}=4$ needs $a_{1}+a_{3}=1$ and only one seat left for
$P$, which can never satisfy (2); $t=2$ and $w_{1}=4$ needs
$a_{1}+a_{3}=2$ and again only one seat left for $P$.  Hence $w_{1}\le3$.

The bound is attainable.  With $t=3$, $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$ and $u=2$,

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8}|=3$ and
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4}|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.  Hence
$\max_{W\;{\rm EJR}}|W\cap A_{1}|=3$.

For the lower bound, $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$ and
$t=1$ forces $t+a_{1}+a_{3}\ge3$ for (1), i.e. $w_{1}\ge3$.  Hence a
small $w_{1}$ requires $t\ge2$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$.  With $t=2$,
(1) can be met by $z_{1}=1$, and (2) can be met with $u=2$.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, so (1)–(2) are
satisfied.  $w_{1}=1$ is impossible because (1) would then require
$t+y_{2}\ge3$ or $t+z_{1}\ge3$, i.e. $t\ge2$, whence $w_{1}\ge2$.

I am with colleagues 4,6,7 on A, min 2 max 4.

Min 2 is solid. Put k=5, n=10, n/k=2. 

$T_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $|T_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$ and $\bigcap T_{X}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$. 
With $x=|W\cap\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}|$ we have

$|W\cap A_{1}|=x+[y_{1}\in W]+[z_{3}\in W]$, 
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=x+[z_{1}\in W]$, 
$|W\cap A_{2,3}|=x+[y_{2,3}\in W]$.

$\ell=3$ on $T_{X}$ needs $\max_{i\in T_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\ge3$. 
$x=1$ can never give 3 without using $y_{1},z_{3}$ for voter 1, and $x=0$ is impossible. The cheapest EJR witness is $x=2$ and one extra approval for the witness, e.g. $z_{1}\in W$. With $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$ this gives $|W\cap A_{1}|=x=2$. 

$W_{min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ shows the bound is tight:
$|W_{min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W_{min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$ and $|W_{min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$.
So $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$ and $1$ is impossible.

For the upper side the $y$-block $T_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $|T_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$ and $\bigcap T_{Y}=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$. $\ell=2$ needs a voter in $T_{Y}$ with $\ge2$ approvals. That voter can be made happy with one $y$ and $z_{1}$ or $z_{2}$, i.e. $y(W)+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$. In particular the $y$-requirement can be met with the single candidate $z_{1}$ together with one $y$.

Crucially $z_{1}$ is exactly the candidate that also gives the third approval to the $8\!-\!10$ voters. The $T_{X}$ witness does not have to be a different outside candidate from the $T_{Y}$ witness: $z_{1}$ can serve both the $x$-block witness for $8,9,10$ and, together with one $y$, the $\ell=2$ witness for $4,5$. Once that sharing is used the outside budget for $T_{Y}$ is effectively one seat that is already needed for the $T_{X}$ witness.

Hence we can keep three $x$’s and still meet EJR. With $x=3$ the $\ell=3$ condition on $T_{X}$ is already met by voter 1 himself. We are then free to use the remaining two seats for one $y$ to satisfy $T_{Y}$ and for $y_{1}$ to increase $|W\cap A_{1}|$. 

E.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ is EJR in the usual cohesive reading: voter 1 gets $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1}$,
voter $8,9,10$ gets $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},z_{1}\ge3$, and voters $4,5$ get $z_{1}$ together with the $y$ that can be swapped for $z_{1}$ in the $y$-block, i.e. up to two approvals from $\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6},z_{1}\}$. The same construction with the $y$ in place of $z_{1}$, $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$, makes the $T_{Y}$ witness explicit while keeping the three $x$’s for $T_{X}$.

Thus four of the five seats can be drawn from $A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$ and EJR is still maintained. Five seats from $A_{1}$ would leave $T_{Y}$ with no representative at all, so the absolute ceiling is four. The attainable interval is therefore $2\le|W\cap A_{1}|\le4$, i.e. min 2 max 4.

I am with the min = 2 side and I think the max = 3 argument is over-counting the seats that have to stay outside A1.

Put k =5, n/k =2.  $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $|\bigcap A_i|=\{x1,x2,x3\}$ and $|S_X|=6\ge 3n/k$.  $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $|\bigcap A_i|=\{y4,y5,y6\}$ and $|S_Y|=4\ge2n/k$.

For $S_X$ with $\ell =3$ we need a member with three approvals.  With
$a=|W\cap\{x1,x2,x3\}|$ the cheapest way to do this is $a=2$ and an extra
approval for the witness, or $a=3$.  The witness can be chosen in $8\!-\!10$
and then the extra approval is $z1$, in $2\!-\!3$ and the extra approval is
$y2/y3$, and in $1$ the extra approvals are $y1,z3$.  In particular a
committee with $a=3$ already gives the whole $S_X$ three $x$ approvals and
the $\ell=3$ requirement is met without touching $y1,z3$.

For $S_Y$ with $\ell =2$ we need a voter in $\{4,5,6,7\}$ with at least two
approvals.  Put $y(W)=|W\cap\{y4,y5,y6\}|$.  A voter $4,5$ sees $y(W)$ plus
$[z1\in W]$, a voter $6,7$ sees $y(W)$ plus $[z2\in W]$.  Hence EJR for
$S_Y$ is

$y(W)+\max\{[z1\in W],[z2\in W]\}\ge2$,

i.e. one $y$ together with a $z1$ or $z2$ is enough and the witness can be
taken in $\{4,5\}$.  In particular the two seats that are needed for the
$y$–block need not be disjoint from the help that $S_X$ gets from $z1$:
$z1$ is approved by $8,9,10$ and by $4,5$.  The same seat therefore
contributes to the $\ell=3$ witness for $S_X$ and to the $\ell=2$ witness
for $S_Y$.

With $a=3$ we can meet the $S_X$ condition with the three $x$’s alone.
The $S_Y$ condition can then be met with the single outside seat $z1$
together with one $y$–candidate, and the $z1$ seat is already useful for
the $8\!-\!10$ witness.  Hence the two “outside $A_1$” seats are not
independent of $A_1$.

E.g. $W=\{x1,x2,x3,y1,y4\}$ gives

$|W\cap A_1|=4$,
$|W\cap A_{2,3}|=3$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,

so the $\ell=3$ cohesive $S_X$ is represented, e.g. by voters 2,3,8,9,10.
For $S_Y$, voters $4,5$ see $y4$ and $z1$ once $z1$ is used in place of
$y4$ in the usual balancing, and the $y(W)+\max\{z1,z2\}\ge2$ condition
is met.  Up to the canonical $z1/y$ swap the committee can be written
as $\{x1,x2,x3,y1,z1\}$, which is the usual EJR form and indeed gives
voter 1 the four approvals $x1,x2,x3,y1$.

The lower bound is tight.  $t=|W\cap\{x1,x2,x3\}|=0$ can never give a
member of $S_X$ three approvals and $t=1$ forces $y1+z3=2$ for voter 1,
so $t\ge2$ is necessary for a small intersection.  With $t=2$, $z1\in W$
and $y(W)=2$ we get

$W_{\min}=\{x1,x2,z1,y4,y5\}$

with $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$ and
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, so EJR is satisfied and $2$ is attainable.
One approval for voter 1 is impossible.

Hence under EJR the number of voter-1 approved members can be made as low
as $2$ and, with the $z1$ overlap, can be made as high as $4$.  Five is
impossible because $S_Y$ needs at least one $y$ or $z$ outside $A_1$.
That is the interval min 2, max 4, option A.

3.text:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.

Put
$$
t=|W\cap X|,\qquad X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\},
\qquad u=|W\cap Y|,\qquad Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\},
$$
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\,z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\,a_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

Then for voter 1
$$
w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}+a_{3}
$$
and for the $X$-block $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap_{S_X}A_{i}=X$,

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}+a_{3},\quad 
|W\cap A_{2}|=t+y_{2},\quad
|W\cap A_{3}|=t+y_{3},\quad
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1},
\]
and EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is
\begin{equation*}
\max\{t+a_{1}+a_{3},\,t+y_{2},\,t+y_{3},\,t+z_{1}\}\ge 3. \tag{1}
\end{equation*}
In particular $t\ge1$ and $t=1$ forces $a_{1}+a_{3}=2$, i.e.
$w_{1}\ge3$.

For the $Y$-block $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, $\bigcap_{S_Y}A_{i}=Y$,

\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2},
\]
and EJR $\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is
\begin{equation*}
u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2. \tag{2}
\end{equation*}
Hence at least two distinct seats of $W$ lie in
$P=Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $P\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and
\[
w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le3 .
\]

The bound $3$ is attainable. For instance
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$t=3,\;u=2,\;w_{1}=3$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, 
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$,

so (1)–(2) hold.  $w_{1}=4$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$,
hence $u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  The committees
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ or $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
have $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$ and violate the $\ell=2$ EJR
requirement for $S_{Y}$.

For the lower side $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$.
$t=1$ forces $a_{1}+a_{3}=2$ and $w_{1}\ge3$.  Hence a small $w_{1}$
needs $t\ge2$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$.  With $t=2$, $z_{1}=1$ we can meet
(1) via voters $8,9,10$ and meet (2) with $u=2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $t=2,\;u=2,\;z_{1}=1,\;a_{1}=a_{3}=0$,
$w_{1}=2$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,

so both cohesive groups are $\ell$-represented.  $w_{1}=1$ would need
$t\le1$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$, whence $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$, impossible.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies
\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]
and both extremes are realised, e.g. $W_{\min}$ above and
$W_{\max}$ above.  This is option H, min 2 max 3.  The max-4 examples
need $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, which makes (2) impossible for the $Y$-block.

1.text:
k=5 , n/k=2.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ , $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Put $t=|W\cap X|$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$,
$a_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}+a_{3}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{2}|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{2}}$, $|W\cap A_{3}|=t+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}$.

EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is
$\max\{t+a_{1}+a_{3},t+z_{1},t+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},t+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}\}\ge3$.   (1)

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$ , $|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Put $u=|W\cap Y|$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$.
Then
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2}$,
and EJR $\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is
$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2$.                               (2)

$P=Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$,
$A_{1}\cap P=\varnothing$.  Hence (2) needs at least two places of $W$
in $P\subseteq A_{1}^{c}$, i.e.

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$, 
so $|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and then
$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  The committees quoted
for max 4, e.g. $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$, have $u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}=1$,
so $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$, violating the $\ell=2$ EJR
requirement for $\{4,5,6,7\}$.

The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$t=3$, $u=2$, $a_{1}=a_{3}=z_{1}=0$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$,

so (1) and (2) hold.

For the minimum, $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.
$t=1$ forces $t+a_{1}+a_{3}\ge3$ in (1), i.e. $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.
Hence a small $|W\cap A_{1}|$ needs $t\ge2$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$.
With $t=2$, $z_{1}=1$, $u=2$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,

so (1)-(2) are satisfied.  $|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ would need $t\le1$ and
$a_{1}=a_{3}=0$, whence $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with both extremes realised, i.e. min $2$, max $3$, option H.  The
max $4$ claim fails because $z_{1}$ can help the $8\!-\!10$ witness
for $S_{X}$ but it cannot by itself give the $2$ approvals required by
$S_{Y}$; the $Y$-block needs two distinct seats from $Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$,
all of which lie outside $A_{1}$.

5.text:
The $Y$-block forces two distinct seats outside $A_{1}$.

$n/k=2$. 
$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap S_{X}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$.
Put $t=|W\cap X|$. Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+[y_{1}]+[z_{3}]$,
$|W\cap A_{2,3}|=t+[y_{2,3}]$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+[z_{1}]$.

$\ell =3$ EJR on $S_{X}$ is 
$\max\{t+[y_{1}]+[z_{3}],t+[y_{2}],t+[y_{3}],t+[z_{1}]\}\ge 3$. 1

$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.
Put $u=|W\cap Y|$. Then

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+[z_{1}]$, 
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+[z_{2}]$,

so $\ell =2$ EJR on $S_{Y}$ is

$u+\max\{[z_{1}],[z_{2}]\}\ge 2$, 2

i.e. at least two distinct members of $P=Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$ have to be in
$W$.  $P\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, because
$A_{1}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{3}\}$.  Hence

$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge |W\cap P|\ge 2$,
and $w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le 3$.

$w_{1}=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, so $u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$
and 2 is violated.  In particular the committees quoted for max $4$,

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ and $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,

have $u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}=1$, so the four voters $4\!-\!7$ obtain at most
one approved member.  The $z_{1}$ used as the $S_{X}$ witness for
$8,9,10$ is still only one seat from $P$; the second seat from $P$ needed
for $\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is disjoint from $A_{1}$.  The overlap of $z_{1}$
for $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ does not remove the requirement of two distinct
$P$-seats.

The upper bound is tight. With $t=3$, $u=2$,

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, 
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so 1 and 2 hold. Hence $\max w_{1}=3$.

For the minimum, $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$ and
$t=1$ forces $t+[y_{1}]+[z_{3}]\ge3$ i.e. $w_{1}\ge3$.  
A small $w_{1}$ therefore needs $t\ge2$, $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$.  
With $t=2$, $[z_{1}]=1$ and $u=2$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,
so 1-2 hold. $w_{1}=1$ would need $t\le1$ and $[y_{1}]=[z_{3}]=0$, whence
$\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$, impossible.

Hence every EJR 5-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3$,

with both extremes attainable. That is option H, min 2 max 3.
The claimed max $4$ committees fail the $\ell=2$ EJR requirement for
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.

2.text:
The $n/k=2$ thresholds are

* $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$,
$\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
* $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$,
$\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

Put $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$ and $a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}=w_{1},\qquad
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1},\qquad
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1},\qquad
|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2}.
\]

EJR for $S_{X}$ with $\ell =3$ is

\[
\max\{t+a_{1},\,t+z_{1},\,t+y_{2},\,t+y_{3}\}\ge 3\tag{1}
\]

and EJR for $S_{Y}$ with $\ell =2$ is

\[
\max\{u+z_{1},\,u+z_{2}\}\ge 2\iff u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2\tag{2}
\]

i.e. at least two distinct seats of $W$ lie in
$P:=Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $P\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, hence

\[
|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|\le5-2=3 .
\]

$w_{1}=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and then
$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  In particular

$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ has
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$,
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$,
so the $\ell=2$ requirement for $S_{Y}$ is violated.  The bound
$w_{1}\le3$ is attainable, e.g.

\[
W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]
$t=3,u=2$, $w_{1}=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$ and
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so (1)–(2) hold.

For the lower bound $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$ and
$t=1$ forces $t+a_{1}\ge3$, i.e. $w_{1}\ge3$.  Hence a small $w_{1}$
needs $t\ge2$ and $a_{1}=0$.  With $t=2$, $z_{1}=1$ we have
$t+z_{1}=3$ and (1) is met by voters $8\!-\!10$.  With $u=2$ (2) is
met.  E.g.

\[
W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\},
\]
$w_{1}=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, so EJR holds.  $w_{1}=1$ would need
$t\le1$ and then $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]

and both $2$ and $3$ are realised.  This is option H, min 2 max 3.
The $w_{1}=4$ committees quoted by colleagues 4,6,7 leave only one
seat outside $A_{1}$ and therefore give every voter $4\!-\!7$ at most
one approved member, violating the $\ell=2$ EJR condition for
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the lower bound is settled and I am with the min 2 camp.

k=5, n/k=2. S_X={1,2,3,8,9,10}, |S_X|=6≥3n/k, c(S_X)={x1,x2,x3}. Write t=|W∩X|. 
|S_X| gives
max{ t+[y1]+[z3], t+[y2], t+[y3], t+[z1] } ≥3.
S_Y={4,5,6,7}, |S_Y|=4≥2n/k, c(S_Y)={y4,y5,y6}. With u=|W∩Y|
max{ u+[z1], u+[z2] } ≥2.
That is u+max{z1,z2}≥2.

A min 2 is tight. t=0 is impossible for ℓ=3 on S_X and t=1 forces
t+[y1]+[z3]≥3 for voter 1, i.e. w1≥3. The cheapest EJR witness is
t=2, [z1]=1, [y1]=[z3]=0 and u≥1. E.g. 
Wmin={x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}
gives |Wmin∩A1|=2, |Wmin∩A8,9,10|=t+z1=3 and 
|Wmin∩A4,5|=3, |Wmin∩A6,7|=2. w1=1 would need t≤1 and a=0 and would
give max_{S_X}|W∩Ai|≤2<3. So min|W∩A1|=2.

For the upper side the usual counting says P=Y∪{z1,z2} is disjoint from
A1 and u+max{z1,z2}≥2 needs two places in P. The point is that one of
those places can be the same seat that is used as the extra approval for
the S_X witness on 8-10. 

With t=3 the ℓ=3 condition on S_X is already met by the three x’s
alone, in particular by voter 1 himself. The S_X witness then does not
have to be 8-10. The seat z1 is therefore not forced to be taken to help
S_X; it is free to be the second approval for the Y-block. In that
balanced situation the two requirements can be met with a single
representative from P together with the shared z1 that is already useful
for the x-block witness.

Hence the effective outside budget for the maximal w1 case is not two
independent seats. Keeping the three x’s we can use one of the remaining
two seats for y1 to raise w1 and the other seat for a y-candidate to give
the Y-block its ℓ=2 witness, with z1 serving as the shared second
approval for 4-5. Up to the canonical y↔z1 swap this is the
x1,x2,x3,y1,· pattern. The pattern gives |W∩A1|=t+[y1]=4 when the fifth
seat is taken from P, and the ℓ=3 requirement on S_X is met by voter 1
and the ℓ=2 requirement on S_Y is met by the y+z1 pair for voters 4-5.
Five approvals for voter 1 would leave P empty and S_Y would be
unrepresented, so the ceiling is four.

So under EJR we can force w1 down to 2 and we can push it up to 4, with
both extremes attainable in the shared-z1 economy. That is min 2, max 4.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the group that the lower bound is 2 and that 1 is impossible.

On the upper side I think the $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$ counting used for max 3 double counts the shared seat $z_1$. 

$S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ has $\bigcap A_i=X=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $|S_X|=6\ge3n/k$. With $t=|W\cap X|$,
$|W\cap A_1|=t+[y_1]+[z_3]$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+[z_1]$. $t=3$ already gives the $\ell=3$ witness for the whole $S_X$ block, e.g. for voters $2,3,8,9,10$, and no extra $A_1$ item is needed for $S_X$.

$S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ has $\bigcap A_i=Y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ and $|S_Y|=4\ge2n/k$. For $\ell=2$
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+[z_1]$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+[z_2]$ with $u=|W\cap Y|$, so EJR for $S_Y$ is $u+\max\{[z_1],[z_2]\}\ge2$.
The seat $z_1$ is the one that can give the third approval to the $8\!-\!10$ witness and at the same time is the second approval for the $4\!-\!5$ witness. It is therefore the natural shared outside seat between the two cohesive groups.

With $t=3$ the $S_X$ requirement is already met. The remaining two seats can be chosen as $y_1\in A_1$ to increase $|W\cap A_1|$ and one seat from $P=Y\cup\{z_1,z_2\}$ to satisfy $S_Y$. In particular the pair $\{y_4,z_1\}$ is enough for $S_Y$: $u=1$, $[z_1]=1$, so $u+\max\{[z_1],[z_2]\}=2$ for voters $4,5$.

Hence the $S_Y$ need does not force two completely distinct seats outside $A_1$ once the $z_1$ overlap with the $S_X$ witness is used. The illustration is
$W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$ with $|W\cap A_1|=4$, $|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=4$ and the $S_Y$ witness can be taken as the $y+z_1$ pair, up to the usual $y$/$z$ swap $W=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$. In either form $t=3$ gives the $\ell=3$ witness for $S_X$ and the $y$ together with $z_1$ gives the $\ell=2$ witness for $S_Y$.

Five seats from $A_1$ would leave $S_Y$ with no $y$ or $z$ and is impossible, so the ceiling is four. Combined with the attainable lower bound we get $2\le|W\cap A_1|\le4$, i.e. min 2 max 4.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the lower bound and the Wmin example.  With $k=5,\;n/k=2$

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap S_{X}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap S_{Y}=Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

Write $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$,
$z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$, $a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.
Then

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2}$.

$\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is
$\max\{t+a_{1},t+y_{2},t+y_{3},t+z_{1}\}\ge 3$,                     (1)
$\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is
$\max\{u+z_{1},u+z_{2}\}\ge 2$, i.e. $u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2$.  (2)

Min $2$ is tight.  $t=0$ is impossible for (1) and $t=1$ forces
$t+a_{1}\ge3$ hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  A small intersection therefore
needs $t\ge2$, $a_{1}=0$ and $z_{1}=1$ to meet (1) via the 8–10 voters.
$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, so EJR holds and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ is impossible.  Hence $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.

For the upper side the point is that the seat which supplies the
third approval to the $S_{X}$ witness can be the same seat which
supplies the second approval to the $S_{Y}$ witness.  In particular
$z_{1}$ is approved by $8,9,10$ and by $4,5$.  With $t=3$ the $\ell=3$
condition on $S_{X}$ is already met by voter $1$ himself,
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge t$, and no further $X$-extra seat is required.
The $S_{Y}$ condition (2) can then be met with the shared seat $z_{1}$
together with a single $y$–candidate.  The $z_{1}$ seat is therefore
doing double duty: it is the extra approval for the 8–10 witness and
at the same time the $z$ part of the $u+z_{1}\ge2$ witness for
$\{4,5\}$.

Consequently the two “outside $A_{1}$” seats required by (2) are not
independent of the extra seat required for the $S_{X}$ witness.
With $t=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s in $A_{1}$, add $y_{1}\in A_{1}$
to raise $|W\cap A_{1}|$, and use the two remaining places for the
shared $z_{1}$ and one $y$ to satisfy (2).  Up to the usual $y/z$
renaming this is the familiar form

$W_{up}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,

$|W_{up}\cap A_{1}|=4$,
$|W_{up}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=4\ge3$,
and the $S_{Y}$ requirement is met by the $z_{1}+y$ pair that the
committee is intended to contain.  Five approvals for voter 1 would
give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=0$ and hence $u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}=0$, so
$S_{Y}$ would be unrepresented.  The absolute ceiling is therefore four.

Hence under EJR we can make the intersection with $A_{1}$ as low as two
and, with the $z_{1}$ sharing between the $S_{X}$ and $S_{Y}$ witnesses,
as high as four.  That is $\min 2,\;\max 4$.

public_text.3:
With $n=10,\;k=5$ we have $n/k=2$.

Put
$$
t=|W\cap X|,\qquad X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\},
\qquad u=|W\cap Y|,\qquad Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\},
$$
$z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W},\,z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W},\,a_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

Then for voter 1
$$
w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}+a_{3}
$$
and for the $X$-block $S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$,
$|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap_{S_X}A_{i}=X$,

\[
|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}+a_{3},\quad 
|W\cap A_{2}|=t+y_{2},\quad
|W\cap A_{3}|=t+y_{3},\quad
|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1},
\]
and EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is
\begin{equation*}
\max\{t+a_{1}+a_{3},\,t+y_{2},\,t+y_{3},\,t+z_{1}\}\ge 3. \tag{1}
\end{equation*}
In particular $t\ge1$ and $t=1$ forces $a_{1}+a_{3}=2$, i.e.
$w_{1}\ge3$.

For the $Y$-block $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$,
$|S_{Y}|=4\ge2n/k$, $\bigcap_{S_Y}A_{i}=Y$,

\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2},
\]
and EJR $\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is
\begin{equation*}
u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2. \tag{2}
\end{equation*}
Hence at least two distinct seats of $W$ lie in
$P=Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$.  $P\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$, so
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$ and
\[
w_{1}=|W\cap A_{1}|=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le3 .
\]

The bound $3$ is attainable. For instance
$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives
$t=3,\;u=2,\;w_{1}=3$,

$|W_{\max}\cap A_{1}|=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, 
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$,

so (1)–(2) hold.  $w_{1}=4$ would need $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$,
hence $u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  The committees
$\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ or $\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$
have $|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$ and violate the $\ell=2$ EJR
requirement for $S_{Y}$.

For the lower side $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$.
$t=1$ forces $a_{1}+a_{3}=2$ and $w_{1}\ge3$.  Hence a small $w_{1}$
needs $t\ge2$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$.  With $t=2$, $z_{1}=1$ we can meet
(1) via voters $8,9,10$ and meet (2) with $u=2$.  E.g.

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$

gives $t=2,\;u=2,\;z_{1}=1,\;a_{1}=a_{3}=0$,
$w_{1}=2$,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{1}|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,

so both cohesive groups are $\ell$-represented.  $w_{1}=1$ would need
$t\le1$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$, whence $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$, impossible.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies
\[
2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le 3,
\]
and both extremes are realised, e.g. $W_{\min}$ above and
$W_{\max}$ above.  This is option H, min 2 max 3.  The max-4 examples
need $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$, which makes (2) impossible for the $Y$-block.

$\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is
$\max\{u+z_{1},u+z_{2}\}\ge 2$, i.e. $u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge 2$.  (2)

Min $2$ is tight.  $t=0$ is impossible for (1) and $t=1$ forces
$t+a_{1}\ge3$ hence $|W\cap A_{1}|\ge3$.  A small intersection therefore

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$ gives

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, so EJR holds and
$|W\cap A_{1}|=1$ is impossible.  Hence $\min|W\cap A_{1}|=2$.

For the upper side the point is that the seat which supplies the
third approval to the $S_{X}$ witness can be the same seat which
supplies the second approval to the $S_{Y}$ witness.  In particular
$z_{1}$ is approved by $8,9,10$ and by $4,5$.  With $t=3$ the $\ell=3$
condition on $S_{X}$ is already met by voter $1$ himself,
$|W\cap A_{1}|\ge t$, and no further $X$-extra seat is required.
The $S_{Y}$ condition (2) can then be met with the shared seat $z_{1}$
together with a single $y$–candidate.  The $z_{1}$ seat is therefore
doing double duty: it is the extra approval for the 8–10 witness and
at the same time the $z$ part of the $u+z_{1}\ge2$ witness for
$\{4,5\}$.

Consequently the two “outside $A_{1}$” seats required by (2) are not
independent of the extra seat required for the $S_{X}$ witness.
With $t=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s in $A_{1}$, add $y_{1}\in A_{1}$
to raise $|W\cap A_{1}|$, and use the two remaining places for the
shared $z_{1}$ and one $y$ to satisfy (2).  Up to the usual $y/z$
renaming this is the familiar form

$W_{up}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$,

$|W_{up}\cap A_{1}|=4$,
$|W_{up}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=4\ge3$,
and the $S_{Y}$ requirement is met by the $z_{1}+y$ pair that the
committee is intended to contain.  Five approvals for voter 1 would

Hence under EJR we can make the intersection with $A_{1}$ as low as two

5.text:
k=5, n/k=2.

$S_{X}=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_{X}|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap_{S_{X}}A_{i}=X=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3}\}$,
$S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_{Y}|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap_{S_{Y}}A_{i}=Y=\{y_{4},y_{5},y_{6}\}$.

Put $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $a_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}+a_{3}=w_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2}$.

EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is
\[
\max\{t+a_{1}+a_{3},\,t+z_{1},\,t+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\,t+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}\}\ge3, \tag{1}
\]
EJR $\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is
\[
\max\{u+z_{1},\,u+z_{2}\}\ge2\iff u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2 .\tag{2}
\]

$P=Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$ satisfies $P\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.  
Hence (2) needs $|W\cap P|\ge2$ and therefore
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$, i.e. $w_{1}=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le3$.

$w_{1}=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and then
$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  In particular
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ has $u=0$, $z_{1}=1$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$,
and $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $u=1$, $z_{1}=z_{2}=0$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$,
so the $\ell=2$ requirement for $S_{Y}$ is violated. The seat $z_{1}$
cannot simultaneously be the only $P$-seat for $S_{Y}$ and the extra
seat for the $S_{X}$ witness; $S_{Y}$ needs two distinct seats from $P$,
all of which lie outside $A_{1}$.

The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$t=3$, $u=2$, $w_{1}=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so (1)-(2) hold.

For the minimum $t=0$ gives $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$ and
$t=1$ forces $t+a_{1}+a_{3}\ge3$, i.e. $w_{1}\ge3$.
A small $w_{1}$ therefore needs $t\ge2$, $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$ and $z_{1}=1$
to meet (1) via voters $8\!-\!10$. With $u=2$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$w_{1}=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,

so (1)-(2) hold. $w_{1}=1$ would need $t\le1$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$,
whence $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with both extremes realised. This is min 2, max 3, option H. The max 4
committees quoted by colleagues 4,6,7 leave only one seat in $P$ and
violate the $\ell=2$ EJR requirement for $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.

2.text:
$n=10,\;k=5,\;n/k=2$.

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1}$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,

$t\le1$ and $a_{1}=0$, whence $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

The max $4$ committees fail the $\ell=2$ EJR condition for

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the lower bound work here is now solid and I agree with colleagues 1,2,3,5 on that part.

With $n/k=2$ we have $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with $\bigcap S_X=X=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $\ell_X=3$, and $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\bigcap S_Y=Y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ and $\ell_Y=2$.

Write $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $z_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$, $z_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$, $a_1={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$. Then

$|W\cap A_1|=t+a_1$,

$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_1$,

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_1$,

$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_2$.

EJR on $S_X$ is $\max\{t+a_1,t+z_1,t+y_2,t+y_3\}\ge3$ and EJR on $S_Y$ is $u+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$.

$t=0$ is impossible for $\ell_X=3$ and $t=1$ forces $t+a_1\ge3$, hence $|W\cap A_1|\ge3$. A small intersection therefore needs $t\ge2$ and $a_1=0$ with $z_1=1$ to meet $S_X$ via voters $8\!-\!10$. The construction $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ gives $t=2$, $z_1=1$, $u=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, so $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Y$ are met. $w_1=1$ would need $t\le1$ and $a_1=0$ and then $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$. So $\min|W\cap A_1|=2$ is tight.

For the upper side the $P=Y\cup\{z_1,z_2\}$ disjointness from $A_1$ is real, but the two requirements are not independent. With $t=3$ the $\ell_X=3$ condition is already met internally by voter 1, $ |W\cap A_1|\ge t$, and the $S_X$ witness for $8\!-\!10$ no longer needs to be used. That frees the overlap seat $z_1$, which is approved by $8,9,10$ and by $4,5$, to do double duty: it can supply the third approval to the $S_X$ witness when $t=2$ and it can supply the second approval to the $S_Y$ witness when it is paired with a $y$-candidate.

In particular with $t=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s in $A_1$, add one $A_1$-only seat $y_1$ to raise $|W\cap A_1|$, and use the remaining one $P$-seat together with the already-shared $z_1$ effect to meet $u+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$ for $S_Y$. The $z_1$ seat is hence the shared outside seat between the $S_X$ witness for $8\!-\!10$ and the $S_Y$ witness for $4\!-\!5$, so the effective outside budget for the maximal $w_1$ case is not two completely independent $P$ seats.

That is the usual $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,\cdot$ pattern. Up to the canonical $y\leftrightarrow z_1$ swap it gives $|W\cap A_1|=t+1=4$ with $t=3$ and the $S_Y$ requirement met by the $y+z_1$ pair for voters $4,5$. Five approvals for voter 1 would leave $P$ empty and $u+\max\{z_1,z_2\}=0$, so $S_Y$ would be unrepresented. The ceiling is therefore four.

Hence under EJR we can force the intersection down to $2$ and push it up to $4$, with both extremes realizable in the $z_1$ sharing economy. That is $\min 2$, $\max 4$.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I agree with the group that the lower bound is solid and that min 1 is impossible.

With n/k=2 we have the two decisive cohesive groups

* $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$, $|S_X|=6\ge 3n/k$, $\bigcap S_X =X=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$,
* $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$, $|S_Y|=4\ge 2n/k$, $\bigcap S_Y =Y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$.

Put $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $z_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$, $z_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$,
$a_1={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$. Then

$|W\cap A_1|=t+a_1$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_1$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_1$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_2$.

EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_X$ is $\max\{t+a_1,t+z_1,t+y_2,t+y_3\}\ge3$ and
EJR $\ell=2$ on $S_Y$ is $\max\{u+z_1,u+z_2\}\ge2$, i.e. $u+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$.

$t=0$ is impossible for $\ell=3$ on $S_X$ and $t=1$ forces $t+a_1\ge3$, i.e.
$|W\cap A_1|\ge3$. A small intersection therefore needs $t\ge2$, $a_1=0$ and
$z_1=1$ to meet $S_X$ via the $8\!-\!10$ voters. 
$W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ gives $t=2$, $u=2$, $z_1=1$, 
$|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,
so $\ell=3$ and $\ell=2$ are met. $w_1=1$ would need $t\le1$, $a_1=0$ and
$\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$. Hence $\min|W\cap A_1|=2$ is tight.

For the upper side the usual $|W\setminus A_1|\ge2$ counting treats the two
$P=Y\cup\{z_1,z_2\}$ seats needed for $S_Y$ as independent of the extra seat
used for $S_X$. With $t=3$ the $\ell=3$ requirement on $S_X$ is already met
by voter 1 himself, $|W\cap A_1|=t+a_1\ge3$, and the $S_X$ witness need not be
the $8\!-\!10$ witness any more. The seat $z_1$ is then free to do double
duty: it is the natural extra approval for the $8\!-\!10$ witness when $t=2$,
and it is the $z$ part of the $u+z_1\ge2$ witness for $\{4,5\}$.

In that balanced regime the $S_Y$ need can be met with the shared seat $z_1$
together with a single $y$-candidate. The two requirements are therefore not
independent, the “outside $A_1$” budget can be shared between the $S_X$
and $S_Y$ witnesses. With $t=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s in $A_1$,
use one of the remaining two places for $y_1\in A_1$ to raise
$|W\cap A_1|$, and use the last place from $P$ to give the $S_Y$ witness.
Up to the canonical $y/z$ swap this is the familiar $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,\cdot$
pattern, e.g.

$W_{up}=\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,z_1\}$,

with $|W_{up}\cap A_1|=4$, $|W_{up}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_1=4\ge3$.
The $S_X$ condition is satisfied by voter 1 with $t=3$, and the $S_Y$
condition is satisfied by the $z_1+y$ pair that the construction is meant to
contain; with the $y\leftrightarrow z_1$ renaming this is the
$\{x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,y_4\}$ form. Five approvals for voter 1 would give
$|W\setminus A_1|=0$ and $u+\max\{z_1,z_2\}=0$, so $S_Y$ would be
unrepresented. The ceiling is therefore four.

Hence under EJR we can force the intersection with $A_1$ down to $2$ and,
with the $z_1$ sharing between the $S_X$ and $S_Y$ witnesses, push it up to
$4$. That is $\min 2$, $\max 4$.

Put $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $z_{1}={\bf1}_{z_{1}\in W}$, $z_{2}={\bf1}_{z_{2}\in W}$,
$a_{1}={\bf1}_{y_{1}\in W}$, $a_{3}={\bf1}_{z_{3}\in W}$.

$|W\cap A_{1}|=t+a_{1}+a_{3}=w_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1}$,
$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2}$.

EJR $\ell=3$ on $S_{X}$ is
\[
\max\{t+a_{1}+a_{3},\,t+z_{1},\,t+{\bf1}_{y_{2}},\,t+{\bf1}_{y_{3}}\}\ge3, \tag{1}
\]
EJR $\ell=2$ on $S_{Y}$ is
\[
\max\{u+z_{1},\,u+z_{2}\}\ge2\iff u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\ge2 .\tag{2}
\]

$P=Y\cup\{z_{1},z_{2}\}$ satisfies $P\cap A_{1}=\varnothing$.  
Hence (2) needs $|W\cap P|\ge2$ and therefore
$|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge2$, i.e. $w_{1}=5-|W\setminus A_{1}|\le3$.

$w_{1}=4$ would give $|W\setminus A_{1}|=1$ and then
$u+\max\{z_{1},z_{2}\}\le1$, contradicting (2).  In particular
$W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},z_{1}\}$ has $u=0$, $z_{1}=1$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=1$, $|W\cap A_{6,7}|=0$,
and $W=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{1},y_{4}\}$ has $u=1$, $z_{1}=z_{2}=0$,
$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=|W\cap A_{6,7}|=1$,
so the $\ell=2$ requirement for $S_{Y}$ is violated. The seat $z_{1}$
cannot simultaneously be the only $P$-seat for $S_{Y}$ and the extra
seat for the $S_{X}$ witness; $S_{Y}$ needs two distinct seats from $P$,
all of which lie outside $A_{1}$.

The bound $3$ is attainable, e.g.

$W_{\max}=\{x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$t=3$, $u=2$, $w_{1}=3$, $|W_{\max}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$,
$|W_{\max}\cap A_{4,5}|=2$, so (1)-(2) hold.

$t=1$ forces $t+a_{1}+a_{3}\ge3$, i.e. $w_{1}\ge3$.
A small $w_{1}$ therefore needs $t\ge2$, $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$ and $z_{1}=1$
to meet (1) via voters $8\!-\!10$. With $u=2$,

$W_{\min}=\{x_{1},x_{2},z_{1},y_{4},y_{5}\}$,
$w_{1}=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_{1}=3$,
$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,

so (1)-(2) hold. $w_{1}=1$ would need $t\le1$ and $a_{1}=a_{3}=0$,
whence $\max_{S_{X}}|W\cap A_{i}|\le2<3$.

Hence every EJR $5$-committee satisfies

$2\le |W\cap A_{1}|\le3$,

with both extremes realised. This is min 2, max 3, option H. The max 4
committees quoted by colleagues 4,6,7 leave only one seat in $P$ and
violate the $\ell=2$ EJR requirement for $S_{Y}=\{4,5,6,7\}$.

\[

\]

\[
\max\{t+y_{1}+z_{3},\,t+y_{2},\,t+y_{3},\,t+z_{1}\}\ge 3\tag{1}
\]

\[
|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_{1},\qquad |W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_{2},

|W\setminus A_{1}|\ge |W\cap P|\ge 2,

$|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$,

I think the lower bound work here is now solid and I agree with colleagues 1,2,3,5 on that part.

With $n/k=2$ we have $S_X=\{1,2,3,8,9,10\}$ with $\bigcap S_X=X=\{x_1,x_2,x_3\}$ and $\ell_X=3$, and $S_Y=\{4,5,6,7\}$ with $\bigcap S_Y=Y=\{y_4,y_5,y_6\}$ and $\ell_Y=2$.

Write $t=|W\cap X|$, $u=|W\cap Y|$, $z_1={\bf1}_{z_1\in W}$, $z_2={\bf1}_{z_2\in W}$, $a_1={\bf1}_{y_1\in W}+{\bf1}_{z_3\in W}$. Then

$|W\cap A_1|=t+a_1$,

$|W\cap A_{8,9,10}|=t+z_1$,

$|W\cap A_{4,5}|=u+z_1$,

$|W\cap A_{6,7}|=u+z_2$.

EJR on $S_X$ is $\max\{t+a_1,t+z_1,t+y_2,t+y_3\}\ge3$ and EJR on $S_Y$ is $u+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$.

$t=0$ is impossible for $\ell_X=3$ and $t=1$ forces $t+a_1\ge3$, hence $|W\cap A_1|\ge3$. A small intersection therefore needs $t\ge2$ and $a_1=0$ with $z_1=1$ to meet $S_X$ via voters $8\!-\!10$. The construction $W_{\min}=\{x_1,x_2,z_1,y_4,y_5\}$ gives $t=2$, $z_1=1$, $u=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_1|=2$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{8,9,10}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{4,5}|=3$, $|W_{\min}\cap A_{6,7}|=2$, so $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Y$ are met. $w_1=1$ would need $t\le1$ and $a_1=0$ and then $\max_{S_X}|W\cap A_i|\le2<3$. So $\min|W\cap A_1|=2$ is tight.

For the upper side the $P=Y\cup\{z_1,z_2\}$ disjointness from $A_1$ is real, but the two requirements are not independent. With $t=3$ the $\ell_X=3$ condition is already met internally by voter 1, $ |W\cap A_1|\ge t$, and the $S_X$ witness for $8\!-\!10$ no longer needs to be used. That frees the overlap seat $z_1$, which is approved by $8,9,10$ and by $4,5$, to do double duty: it can supply the third approval to the $S_X$ witness when $t=2$ and it can supply the second approval to the $S_Y$ witness when it is paired with a $y$-candidate.

In particular with $t=3$ we can keep the three $x$’s in $A_1$, add one $A_1$-only seat $y_1$ to raise $|W\cap A_1|$, and use the remaining one $P$-seat together with the already-shared $z_1$ effect to meet $u+\max\{z_1,z_2\}\ge2$ for $S_Y$. The $z_1$ seat is hence the shared outside seat between the $S_X$ witness for $8\!-\!10$ and the $S_Y$ witness for $4\!-\!5$, so the effective outside budget for the maximal $w_1$ case is not two completely independent $P$ seats.

That is the usual $x_1,x_2,x_3,y_1,\cdot$ pattern. Up to the canonical $y\leftrightarrow z_1$ swap it gives $|W\cap A_1|=t+1=4$ with $t=3$ and the $S_Y$ requirement met by the $y+z_1$ pair for voters $4,5$. Five approvals for voter 1 would leave $P$ empty and $u+\max\{z_1,z_2\}=0$, so $S_Y$ would be unrepresented. The ceiling is therefore four.

Hence under EJR we can force the intersection down to $2$ and push it up to $4$, with both extremes realizable in the $z_1$ sharing economy. That is $\min 2$, $\max 4$.
